A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same PoisonedFL study. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on five datasets, including attack comparisons, ablations, adaptive countermeasure experiments, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark experiments, countermeasure evaluations, ablations, and appendix results.

M1.justification: PoisonedFL retains the fixed random sign vector, adaptive magnitude vector, and hypothesis-testing-based scaling adjustment. The tailored defenses and adaptive attack procedures in Section 7 are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, FashionMNIST, Purchase, CIFAR-10, and FEMNIST, with the same synthetic-data and client-participation scenarios. Dataset descriptions move from v1 Appendix B.1 to v2 Section 6.1.1 without changing coverage.

E2.justification: The seven comparator attacks, eight defenses, FedAvg control, and synthetic-data Fang/Min-Max comparisons are retained. M-Krum, N-Bound, and FLDet are abbreviations of existing defenses, not new comparators.

E3.justification: Data splits, model architectures, client counts, participation rates, training budgets, learning rates, metrics, and countermeasure settings remain unchanged. Removing the duplicated evaluation-metric subsection does not alter the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the FL-setting sweeps, magnitude and scaling ablations, adaptive evasion experiments, normalization test, synthetic-data analysis, and Appendix A mechanism and random-sign analyses. No analytical experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 6–7 retain the same mean and standard-deviation reporting across rounds. Appendix A.2 and Table 8 retain the six random sign-vector seeds, numbered 1–6. No uncertainty-reporting or repetition practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–8 and the plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains testing errors of 53.86% for PoisonedFL and 70.02% for Fang on Purchase with TrMean, preserving that ranking.

T1.justification: The optimization formulations, magnitude-update equations, binomial hypothesis-test reasoning, and detector/adaptive-attack definitions remain mathematically unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims about multi-round consistency, minimal attacker knowledge, outperforming seven attacks, and breaking eight defenses. The shortened title does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of self-cancellation, defense failure, adaptive evasion, and normalization limits are retained. Section 8 preserves the synthetic-data interpretation and the limitation that attacks are harder to apply to cross-silo FL.

D1.justification: Implementation details, architectures, hyperparameters, and hardware information are preserved. Dataset descriptions move into Section 6.1.1, and the disclosure of 16 GeForce RTX 3090 GPUs moves to Appendix B.1; neither is newly disclosed.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 40 works and retain the same research positioning. Reference reordering, renumbering, author-name formatting, and bibliographic metadata changes do not alter the cited research.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the title, updates author and affiliation text, removes ACM template boilerplate and the duplicate metric subsection, and moves dataset descriptions into the main experimental setup. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The entire document changes from an ACM two-column format to a single-column layout, with different typography and resized or relocated figures and tables. Figures 8–9 rearrange six horizontal plots into two rows across three defenses; Figures 3–6 abbreviate defense labels. The underlying results are retained.

improvement.justification: Removing duplicated metric text and ACM placeholders, and placing dataset descriptions in the main setup, provides modest editorial benefits. However, the reformatting also makes Table 1 and several plots smaller. With the scientific reasoning, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged, these presentation tradeoffs leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
